claims.statement: Jem Mace was touring with a view to meeting Tom Allen in the ring, and the text is garbled at this point.
Talk of another match between Tom Allen and Mike McCoole said their names were mentioned as probable contestants.
Johnny Franklin brought Tom Allen and Coburn together at New Orleans for a match.
Thomas Bascom of Marysville, Tennessee, offered to bet Tom Allen $10,000 that he could beat him inside eight rounds.
Thomas Bascom offered to bet Tom Allen, or any other man, $5,000 or more that Charley Gallagher, after two hours' training with Bascom, could whip his opponent inside twenty rounds.
Tom Allen challenged Mike McCoole to fight him within the ring after the Gallagher defeat.
A New York dispatch reported that Joe Coburn said he would fight Tom Allen within four months.
Tom Allen said that if he won his fight with Ben Hogan, he would make a match with Ed O'Baldwin for $2,500 or $5,000 a side.
The paper said that had Ned O'Baldwin lived, a contest with Tom Allen would certainly have taken place the next spring.
Jem Mace published a card announcing that he was coming to America to fight Allen for the championship of the world.

Tom Allen had repeatedly said he would never deposit money with an Eastern stakeholder, claiming foul play by certain New York parties, and wanted a Western stakeholder and a Western place for the match.
Joe Goss wrote to Cincinnati of his willingness to fight Tom Allen, and a $500 forfeit was put up for Goss at the Empire saloon in the hands of Eph Holland.
Tom Allen expressed his hope that the fight with Joe Goss would be brought about, and his confidence that he could whip Goss.
Goss had reportedly deposited $500 with Eph Holland to make a match with Allen, a claim the paper doubted.
Sporting circles expected Tom Allen to insist on a fight with Joe Goss within twelve weeks of signing articles.
Some men claiming to be posted said Joe Goss would not agree to a meeting with Tom Allen for four months after signing articles and might stave the match off.
Tom Allen and Joe Goss were to meet in the same ring where Steve Taylor and George Rooke agreed to fight for $1,000 a side.
Tom Allen covered the $500 that Joe Goss deposited with Eph Holland of Cincinnati to make a match for the championship of America and a purse of $1,000 to $5,900 (printed as $5,900).
Jem Mace thought of matching Joe Goss against Tom Allen while Mace was in England.
Jem Mace gave way to Joe Goss, who wanted to fight Tom Allen.
A claim put to Mace says Tom Allen had been in training to fight George Rooke a short time before he made the Goss match.
Ben Hogan says he met Tom Allen, who was spoiling for a fight.
Ben Hogan says he put up the money for a match with Tom Allen (printed as 'nsiieed the money right down').

Allen's conditions for the fight were that it take place within three months of signing the articles, within fifty miles of St. Louis or Pittsburg, under London prize-ring rules but with a sixteen-foot ring.
The proposed match was for $1,000 to $2,500 a side, within 100 miles of New Orleans, within three months after signing articles.
St. Louis sporting men were waiting to hear whether John L. Sullivan would accept Richard K. Fox's challenge on behalf of Tom Allen.
While in England, Tom Allen kept a standing challenge to fight any man in Great Britain.
Allen's challenge set the fight to take place within three months and within 100 miles of New Orleans.
Harry Hill was to be the final stakeholder for the match.
Sullivan wanted his fight with Tom Allen held near Leadville, Colorado, fearing a Louisiana law would send them to the penitentiary.
Eph Holland of Cincinnati imported Joe Goss to America to fight Tom Allen.
